method: Static archive enumeration, source execution-path analysis, AST-only Base64/zlib decoding, upstream byte comparisons, exact original wheel recovery and RECORD verification. No specimen code was executed.

samples.identification: Reduced one-member tar.gz containing LiteLLM 1.107.0 pyproject.toml; not the complete sdist named in its checksum query
samples.reason: The manifest is byte-identical to the independently recovered compromised sdist manifest. Its injected Maturin data=cook setting is the confirmed build-input modification that packages the credential stealer and startup backdoor in the seven original release wheels. Confirmed tampered provenance and changed build semantics tip the verdict; this is not a claim of host credential theft by the manifest itself.
samples.execution: The manifest declares maturin==1.15.0 and a Rust Python bridge, three ordinary CLI entrypoints, core/extras dependencies, and a cook wheel-data directory. This reduced archive supplies neither the project code nor cook contents. It has no standalone executable payload.
samples.coverage_gap: Only notable build and campaign observations are supported. Two distinct hostile/suspicious techniques cannot be established from these bytes; no duplicate or filename-gated conviction is added.

samples.identification: @serifpersia/dango 3.7.1 local anime/media application with Node server and React frontend
samples.reason: The operations form a coherent media, synchronization and Rich Presence application. User-directed Google OAuth/token refresh and explicit Discord self-token setup account for the credential handling. No covert collection, tasking implant, or unrelated secret destination was found.
execution: orchestrator.js parses ports/modes, checks Node version, optionally prompts before an npm update, and spawns the local server/client with controlled argv. Shutdown authenticates a local POST with a random token and terminates its child processes.

The server migrates its own application databases and tokens from prior application directories into its per-user data directory. It loads its own google_tokens.json, refreshes expiring Google access tokens via the configured publisher worker, and uses returned tokens to synchronize application JSON snapshots to the user-authorized Drive folders. The alternate path uses the user-provided Google OAuth client directly.

The published worker holds the application client secret, forwards exchange/refresh grants to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and returns responses. It contains no token storage or second exfiltration sink. The live read-only /auth-url response points to Google consent for drive.appdata, drive.file and userinfo.email, with localhost redirect. This does not prove that the deployed worker is identical to the published source or reveal its private logs.

The settings bookmarklet checks discord.com, accesses webpack token getters, writes the token to the clipboard, and instructs the user to paste/save it to the application. The UI discloses Discord ToS/account risks. The backend stores the configured token in its own .env and uses it with Discord Gateway/API for user-selected activity presence. The accurate suspicious token-acquisition trait remains unchanged.

Provider refresh fetches a publisher GitHub registry, verifies each module against its declared SHA-256, saves it to remote-providers, imports the local file URL, calls its provider factory and validates its interface. All 23 referenced module hashes matched. Seven other registry entries construct media iframe URLs without importing code. Remote updates are a trust dependency but do not establish C2.

All downloaded provider modules were inspected as media search/metadata/stream-resolution adapters. Apparent exec uses are regex matching, and the AnimePahe eval wording is a packed media-player decoder. got-scraping 3.2.9 supplies browser-like HTTP/TLS scraping; its disabled peer verification is dual-use and remains reported.
samples.source_label_explanation: LPM specifically labels the publisher-worker refresh-token relay as credential exfiltration and propagates an earlier version source fingerprint. The relay exists, but the source and live authorization response support an OAuth-broker interpretation. The Discord bookmarklet, dynamic provider import and broker remain security-relevant capabilities.
samples.missing_context: Deployed worker implementation/log retention, future mutable provider/registry content, local LAN deployment and authorization settings are unknown; no malicious deployment is invented.

samples.identification: Original LiteLLM 1.107.0 source distribution: 4709 regular archive members
samples.reason: This is the confirmed tampered source-release build input for the malicious 1.107.0 wheel release. Comparison with upstream verifies the injected data=cook setting. Provenance and build-input tampering tip the artifact verdict, while absent wheel payloads constrain behavior claims.
execution: All Python and Rust executable sources compared byte-for-byte with upstream a8113b0. Of 4709 files, 4394 match exactly; the five non-UI changes are pyproject.toml and four Cargo.toml readme metadata additions. The remaining changes/extras are generated frontend exports and PKG-INFO. Hash manifests, changed-file lists and focused UI comparisons are retained in scratch; this is not a reproducible-build proof for every frontend bundle.

The source contains no cook directory, cook.py, cook.pth, sitecustomize.py or usercustomize.py. Maturin selects the absent cook wheel-data directory; its spelling is retained as an incident marker, not an independent credential-theft behavior.

The Rust build.rs adds ordinary macOS linker arguments. Python initialization applies process defaults, sets up the LLM interface and fetches/validates a JSON model-price catalog; the retrieved reference is JSON data, not source code handed to an evaluator. CLI/proxy credential reads, provider API calls, configured hooks, database operations and frontend code examples fit the advertised gateway purpose.

Pinned companion wheels litellm-enterprise 0.1.78 and litellm-proxy-extras 0.4.110, flagged dependency versions fastapi 0.159.1 and semantic-router 0.3.2, the build backend, and the pinned liteadmin-mcp source reference were recovered. Their relevant entry, import, authentication and request paths were inspected. The inspected companions supply the normal web/LLM/proxy functionality; they do not account for the wheel-only startup implant.
samples.coverage_gap: No local credential stealer, backdoor, or two independent suspicious techniques exist in this sdist. Preserve notable incident build markers and report the classifier miss; do not manufacture hostile traits to meet the minimum.

recovered_malicious_comparison.collector: cook.pth imports cook at Python startup. cook.py Base64-decodes and zlib-decompresses 61000 bytes of Python then execs them. The module starts a daemon-thread collector, reads/decrypts browser secrets, SSH/cloud/CI/developer/AI-tool stores and process environments, queries LiteLLM credential/model tables through a child Python process, and requests cloud metadata credentials. pc_collect_all feeds JSON into AES-CBC encryption; RSA-OAEP wraps the random key. pc_pack builds hdr.json/data.bin/key.bin in a gzip tar and pc_post sends it to the lookalike www.litellm.dev/healthcheck with token/hash headers. A run-once marker is written after successful upload.
recovered_malicious_comparison.loader: sitecustomize.py takes a lock, forks and setsid, redirects descriptors, polls a GitHub dead drop hourly, invokes its embedded collector, downloads http://<resolved domain>/codepy and execs compile(response). Its fork daemon cannot operate as written on Windows, while cook.pth still launches the collector there. The dead-drop fetch returned 404; no second-stage bytes or runtime success are inferred.
recovered_malicious_comparison.coverage: All original hostile/suspicious findings on both recovered loader/collector source files survive unchanged: 12 and 13 finding instances respectively, including decoded layers. Recovered wheels are comparison evidence, not additional supplied samples requiring markers.

trait_changes.preservation: All 11 relocations preserve their predicates, effective scopes, exclusions, criticalities and explicit composite consumers. Unsupported inherited attack/behavior mappings were removed from the neutral observations. All non-moved rules in edited files retain equivalent complete boolean definitions after reference substitution.

unsupported_claims.single lowercase literal line: GraphQL fields and Python example output lines do not establish a shell command or persistence.
unsupported_claims.mouseClick: A Redux action literal establishes no Socket.IO channel or remote command execution.
unsupported_claims.user_location: A web-search request location key does not establish session data collection.
unsupported_claims.victim/session and secret/dump wording: The actual matches describe CSRF protection and keeping non-secret fields out of a key dump; they do not perform victim control or secret theft.
unsupported_claims.SKIP_VERIFY and unrelated getenv: The LiteLLM flag skips a pre-launch proxy key check. A verification-shaped name plus an unrelated getenv does not establish an environment-controlled hash bypass.
unsupported_claims.callback_url: An optional model field declaration establishes no cycle hook, network request or exfiltration.
unsupported_claims.hexadecimal api_key: The actual match is a documented SHA-256 hash example, not a hardcoded exfiltration credential.
unsupported_claims.token mutation and ToS disclosure: Generic mutation-call text and a ToS clause belong to source syntax and natural-language phrasing. The actual Discord token-extraction objective remains unchanged.

trait_changes.php_correction: The old PHP stdin regex matched the XML-processing-instruction regex alternation in Dango. Require a closed quoted snippet and a plausible PHP executable path after the pipe. The real PHP smoke-test fixture still matches, including its existing exclusion of the upload-RCE objective. No other available non-batch source-archive match was found during the external sample audit.
trait_changes.duplicate_removal: Removed the stale suspicious ps-regex-repaired-base64 atom that duplicated the notable powershell-base64-regex-preprocessing predicate and blocked validation before this work. Whitespace cleanup proves no concealment. The exact notable capability and all active consumers remain; the real fragmented batch loader still has its two supported suspicious concealment objectives.
trait_changes.consumers: Exact references and 26 source ancestor-selector occurrences were inspected. Neutral syntax/disclosure observations are not reintroduced as attack objectives through broad directory selectors. Destination ancestors were audited separately. Positive attack chains and the complete validation corpus check retained coverage. The ToS clause is placed under natural-language phrasing so it cannot newly trigger broad documentation exclusions; remaining source-call ancestor membership is PHP-only and disjoint from its JavaScript scope.
trait_changes.evidence_scope: The named external samples directory was inspected for affected matchers without searching other worktrees. No matching positive source members outside this batch were recovered there; existing real batch-loader and PHP-smoke controls and independently recovered original malicious wheels provide positive coverage.

remaining_suspicious_hostile.desc: Bookmarklet copies Discord token from webpack to clipboard

material_losses: Only the false PHP-pipeline finding disappears from Dango (outer archive, server.js and one decoded layer). Every other supplied-sample observation survives under its mapped ID; Dango retains its accurate suspicious token bookmarklet finding. The unfired stale PowerShell duplicate loses unsupported suspicious significance globally; the actual technique remains covered by the retained capability and fragmented-eval composite.
classifier_disagreement: All three supplied samples remain model class 0 / level -1 (benign). This agrees with Dango but misses the two confirmed tampered LiteLLM artifacts. Their bytes support build/incident indicators rather than the absent wheel payload behaviors. No score-inflating traits were added. Scanner 2.13.0 also warns that its model feature spec is v18 while extraction expects v19; model-version limitations are recorded rather than hidden.
